t.7.81.1: When Rāma had thus recounted that wondrous birth of his, Lakṣmaṇa and the greatly renowned Bharata spoke once more.
t.7.81.2: Having then dwelt for a year as the beloved of Soma's son, what did she do, O best of men? You ought to tell me that.
t.7.81.3: Hearing the sweetness of the words of those two as they questioned him, Rāma again told this tale about the son of Prajāpati.
t.7.81.4: When the valiant one had attained manhood, the supremely wise and greatly renowned Budha summoned Saṃvarta, the most noble one.
t.7.81.6: Having gathered together all these friends, who perceived the truth, he who was skilled in speech, well composed and steadfast, spoke to them all.
t.7.81.5: Cyavana, the son of Bhṛgu, and the sage Ariṣṭanemin, Pramodana, the bringer of delight, and then the sage Durvāsas.
t.7.81.7: This mighty-armed one is King Ila, the son of Kardama. Know him as he truly is, and let what is good for him be done.
t.7.81.8: Even while they were conversing, the greatly splendid Kardama came to that hermitage together with the great-souled twice-born.
t.7.81.9: Pulastya and Kratu, and likewise Vaṣaṭkāra, and the greatly radiant Oṃkāra came to that hermitage.
t.7.81.10: Then all of them, glad at heart at meeting one another and wishing the welfare of the lord of Bāhli, each spoke words separately.
t.7.81.11: But Kardama spoke words of supreme benefit for the sake of his son: "O twice-born ones, hear my words, which are indeed for the good of the king."
t.7.81.12: I see no other remedy apart from Vṛṣadhvaja; there is no sacrifice higher than the Aśvamedha, and it is dear indeed to that great-souled one.
t.7.81.13: "Therefore, wholly for the sake of the king, let us worship the unapproachable one." Thus addressed by Kardama, all the bulls among the twice-born approved of that sacrifice for the propitiation of Rudra.
t.7.81.14: But a royal sage, a disciple of Saṃvarta and a conqueror of enemy cities, renowned by the name Marutta, performed that sacrifice.
t.7.81.15: Then a great sacrifice took place near the hermitage of Budha, and the greatly renowned Rudra attained supreme satisfaction.
t.7.81.16: Then, at the completion of the sacrifice, Umāpati, pleased with supreme joy, spoke these words to all the twice-born concerning Ilā.
t.7.81.18: While the lord of the gods was speaking thus, those twice-born ones, with minds well composed, sought to propitiate the lord of the gods so that Ilā might become a man.
t.7.81.17: O best of the twice-born, I am pleased with the horse sacrifice and with the devotion of this lord of Bāhli. What pleasing and auspicious thing shall I do for him?
t.7.81.19: Then Rudra, of very great splendour, his heart pleased, gave manhood back to Ilā, and having given it, he vanished.
t.7.81.21: But the king, abandoning Bāhli, founded in the Madhyadeśa the city of Pratiṣṭhāna, unsurpassed and bringing renown.
t.7.81.20: When the horse sacrifice was completed and Hara had vanished from sight, all the far-seeing twice-born departed the way they had come.
t.7.81.22: Śaśabindu was king in Bāhli, a conqueror of enemy cities, while in Pratiṣṭhāna the mighty Ila, son of Prajāpati, was king.
t.7.81.23: In due time Ila attained the supreme world of Brahmā, and King Purūravā, the son of Ilā, obtained Pratiṣṭhāna.
t.7.81.24: Such indeed is the power of the horse sacrifice, O bulls among men: one who had become a woman regained his manhood, and whatever else is hard to attain.
